original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhiḥ jñānayogavyavasthitiḥ|
dānaṃ damaśca yajñaśca svādhyāyastapa ārjavam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: [The first items of the list that 16.3 calls the divine endowment:] fearlessness (abhaya), purity of one's being (sattva-saṃśuddhi), steadfastness in jñāna-yoga (jñānayoga-vyavasthiti), giving (dāna), self-restraint (dama), sacrifice (yajña), recitation of the Veda (svādhyāya), austerity (tapas) and uprightness (ārjava).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse has no main verb; the list continues through 16.2 and is completed in 16.3 (see the sentence entry tea:bhagavad-gita:16.1-3). The compound jñānayoga-vyavasthiti can be read 'steadfastness in knowledge and yoga' (dvandva) or 'steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge' (cf. 3.3); both readings are kept open. sattva in sattva-saṃśuddhi is one's inner being (commentators: the mind), not the guṇa. Edition: the speaker heading 'śrī bhagavānuvāca' is carried inside the segment text (kept as in the segment).

original.text: ahiṃsā satyamakrodhastyāgaḥ śāntirapaiśunam|dayā bhūteṣvaloluptvaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīracāpalam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: [The list of the divine endowment continues:] non-harm (ahiṃsā), truth (satya), freedom from anger (akrodha), relinquishment (tyāga), peace (śānti), not slandering (apaiśuna), compassion toward beings (dayā), freedom from greed (aloluptva), gentleness (mārdava), modesty (hrī) and steadiness, not fickleness (acāpala).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: No main verb; part of the sentence 16.1–3. aloluptva is also read 'freedom from covetousness'; hrī is shame at wrongdoing, modesty.

original.text:
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucamadroho nātimānitā|
bhavanti sampadaṃ daivīmabhijātasya bhārata
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: [and] vigour (tejas), forbearance (kṣamā), steadfastness (dhṛti), purity (śauca), freedom from malice (adroha) and absence of excessive pride (nātimānitā) — these belong to one born to the divine endowment (daivī sampad), Bhārata.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Completes the list begun at 16.1 (26 qualities in all). abhijāta: 'born toward/for' the endowment — commentators: one born with it as his destiny.

original.text: dambho darpo'bhimānaśca krodhaḥ pāruṣyameva ca|ajñānaṃ cābhijātasya pārtha sampadamāsurīm
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Hypocrisy (dambha), arrogance (darpa), excessive pride (abhimāna), anger (krodha), harshness (pāruṣya) and ignorance (ajñāna) belong to one born to the demonic endowment (āsurī sampad), Pārtha.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: daivī sampadvimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā|mā śucaḥ sampadaṃ daivīmabhijāto'si pāṇḍava
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: The divine endowment is held to lead to release (vimokṣa), the demonic to bondage (nibandha). Do not grieve (mā śucaḥ), Pāṇḍava: you are born to the divine endowment.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'mā śucaḥ' recurs at 18.66; the address answers Arjuna's grief (2.11 ff.).

original.text: dvau bhūtasargau loke'smin daiva āsura eva ca|daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śrṛṇu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: In this world there are two creations of beings (bhūta-sarga): the divine (daiva) and the demonic (āsura). The divine has been told at length; now hear from me, Pārtha, the demonic.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'the divine has been told at length' — commentators refer this to the earlier teaching (e.g. the marks of the one of steady wisdom, 2.55 ff., and 16.1–3). Edition spelling 'śrṛṇu' (for śṛṇu) kept as in the segment.

original.text: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidurāsurāḥ|na śaucaṃ nāpi cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Demonic people do not know either engaging in action (pravṛtti) or refraining from it (nivṛtti); neither purity (śauca), nor right conduct (ācāra), nor truth (satya) is found in them.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: pravṛtti and nivṛtti are taken by commentators as what is to be done and what is to be refrained from; 18.30 uses the same pair for the sāttvic understanding.

original.text: asatyamapratiṣṭhaṃ te jagadāhuranīśvaram|aparasparasambhūtaṃ kimanyatkāmahaitukam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: They say that the world is without truth (asatya), without foundation (apratiṣṭha), without a Lord (anīśvara), not come into being from one another (aparaspara-sambhūta) — 'what else? It has desire (kāma) for its cause.'
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The view is stated only as the view of the demonic, to be rejected; the text names no school. aparaspara-sambhūta is obscure: literally 'not arisen from one another' (i.e. not produced in an ordered causal sequence); Śaṅkara and others read it as 'arisen from the mutual union (of male and female)', which fits the following 'caused by desire'. The minimal literal sense is kept in the paraphrase.

original.text: etāṃ dṛṣṭimavaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno'lpabuddhayaḥ|prabhavantyugrakarmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato'hitāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Holding fast to this view (dṛṣṭi), these ruined selves (naṣṭātman) of small understanding (alpa-buddhi), of cruel deeds, hostile, come forth for the destruction of the world.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: naṣṭātman: 'whose self (ātman) is lost/ruined' — the verse does not say in what sense (commentators: fallen from the means to the other world); kept open. ahitāḥ may mean 'enemies' or 'harmful'.

original.text: kāmamāśritya duṣpūraṃ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ|mohādgṛhītvāsadgrāhānpravartante'śucivratāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Resorting to insatiable desire (kāma), filled with hypocrisy (dambha), pride (māna) and intoxication (mada), having taken up false notions (asad-grāha) through delusion (moha), they set to work with impure vows (aśuci-vrata).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: cintāmaparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntāmupāśritāḥ|kāmopabhogaparamā etāvaditi niśicatāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: [They are] given to boundless anxiety (cintā) that ends only with their dissolution (pralaya), holding the enjoyment of desires as the highest, convinced that this is all there is (etāvat) —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: No main verb of its own: the participles continue the description and lead into 'īhante' in 16.12 (they may also be read with 16.10). pralaya here is the end of life (commentators: death). Edition glitch: 'niśicatāḥ' for niścitāḥ, kept as in the segment.

original.text: āśāpāśaśatairbaddhāḥ kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ|īhante kāmabhogārthamanyāyenārthasañcayān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Bound by hundreds of fetters of hope (āśā-pāśa), given over to desire and anger (kāma-krodha), they strive to amass wealth by unjust means (anyāyena) for the enjoyment of desires.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: idamadya mayā labdhamimaṃ prāpsye manoratham|idamastīdamapi me bhaviṣyati punardhanam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: [They think:] 'This I have gained today; this wish (manoratha) I shall attain; this is mine, and this wealth too will be mine hereafter.'
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Direct speech of the demonic person, framed by 'iti ajñāna-vimohitāḥ' at the end of 16.15; the sentence concludes in 16.16 ('patanti narake').

original.text: asau mayā hataḥ śatrurhaniṣye cāparānapi|īśvaro'hamahaṃ bhogī siddho'haṃ balavānsukhī
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: [They think:] 'That enemy has been slain by me, and I shall slay others too. I am the lord (īśvara), I am the enjoyer, I am accomplished (siddha), strong and happy.'
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Direct speech continued (16.13–15). īśvara and siddha are the self-claims of the deluded, not the text's technical senses.

original.text: āḍhyo'bhijanavānasmi ko'nyo'sti sadṛśo mayā|yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ityajñānavimohitāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: [They think:] 'I am wealthy and of high birth; who else is like me? I shall sacrifice, I shall give, I shall rejoice' — so [think those] deluded by ignorance (ajñāna).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Sacrifice and giving here are done for self-display (cf. 16.17, 17.12, 17.21).

original.text: anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ|prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake'śucau
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Led astray by many thoughts (citta), caught in a net of delusion (moha), attached to the enjoyment of desires, they fall into a foul hell (naraka).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: aneka-citta-vibhrānta: 'bewildered by many (a multitude of) thoughts (citta)'. Main clause of the sentence whose direct speech is 16.13–15.

original.text: ātmasambhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ|yajante nāmayajñaiste dambhenāvidhipūrvakam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Self-conceited (ātma-saṃbhāvita), stubborn (stabdha), filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they sacrifice with sacrifices in name only (nāma-yajña), with hypocrisy (dambha), not according to the rule (avidhi-pūrvakam).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: nāma-yajña: sacrifices that are sacrifices only in name (commentators: or done for the sake of a name/fame).

original.text: ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ|māmātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto'bhyasūyakāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Resorting to ego (ahaṅkāra), force, arrogance (darpa), desire and anger, these carping ones (abhyasūyaka) hate me, [who dwell] in their own bodies and in those of others.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: No finite verb of its own apart from the participles; grammatically it continues the subject of 16.17. 'māṃ ātma-para-deheṣu': the Lord present in their own and others' bodies (cf. 17.6, 18.61). The same list ahaṅkāra–bala–darpa–kāma–krodha recurs at 18.53 as what is to be cast off.

original.text: tānahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrānsaṃsāreṣu narādhamān|kṣipāmyajasramaśubhānāsurīṣveva yoniṣu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Those hateful, cruel, lowest of men, inauspicious ones I ceaselessly cast, in the rounds of rebirth (saṃsāra), into demonic wombs (āsurī yoni).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: asurīṃ yonimāpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani|māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Having entered demonic wombs, deluded birth after birth, never reaching me, Kaunteya, they then go to the lowest state (adhamā gati).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Edition glitch: 'asurīṃ' for āsurīṃ, kept as in the segment.

original.text: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ|kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: This gate of hell (naraka), destructive of the self (ātman), is threefold: desire (kāma), anger (krodha) and greed (lobha). Therefore one should abandon these three.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: nāśanam ātmanaḥ: 'ruinous to oneself/the self' — the verse leaves open in what sense the self is ruined.

original.text: etairvimuktaḥ kaunteya tamodvāraistribhirnaraḥ|ācaratyātmanaḥ śreyastato yāti parāṃ gatim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: A man freed from these three gates of darkness (tamas), Kaunteya, practises the good of the self (ātmanaḥ śreyas) and thereby goes to the highest goal (parā gati).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmanaḥ śreyaḥ: 'the good of the self / one's own good' — the reflexive is kept open.

original.text: yaḥ śāstravidhimutsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ|na sa siddhimavāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: One who casts aside the ordinance of scripture (śāstra-vidhi) and acts on the impulse of desire (kāma-kāra) attains neither perfection (siddhi), nor happiness (sukha), nor the highest goal.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: tasmācchāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kāryākāryavyavasthitau|jñātvā śāstravidhānoktaṃ karma kartumihārhasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Therefore scripture (śāstra) is your authority (pramāṇa) in settling what is to be done and what is not to be done. Knowing what the ordinance of scripture declares, you should do action here.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'iha' ('here') is read by commentators as 'in this world' or 'in this field of action (karma-bhūmi)'. The verse concludes ch. 16 and prompts Arjuna's question at 17.1 about those who sacrifice with faith outside the ordinance.

paraphrase: Chapter 16 (Kṛṣṇa to Arjuna; no question opens it). Structure: (1) 16.1–3 the divine endowment (daivī sampad), twenty-six qualities from fearlessness to absence of excessive pride; (2) 16.4 the demonic endowment (āsurī sampad): hypocrisy, arrogance, excessive pride, anger, harshness, ignorance; (3) 16.5 their results — release and bondage — and the assurance to Arjuna that he is born to the divine one ('do not grieve'); (4) 16.6–20 the two creations of beings and a long portrait of the demonic: their ignorance of what to do and refrain from and their lack of purity, conduct and truth (16.7), their view that the world is without truth, foundation or Lord and caused by desire (16.8), their destructive deeds, insatiable desire, anxiety and unjust getting (16.9–12), their boasting inner speech (16.13–15), their fall into hell (16.16), their sacrifices in name only and hatred of the Lord in all bodies (16.17–18), and the Lord's casting them into demonic wombs birth after birth, down to the lowest state (16.19–20); (5) 16.21–22 desire, anger and greed as the threefold gate of hell, freedom from which leads to the highest goal; (6) 16.23–24 whoever sets aside the ordinance of scripture attains neither perfection, happiness nor the highest goal, so scripture is the authority for what is to be done. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to distinguish the two endowments by their results, reassure Arjuna, and direct him to act by the authority of scripture.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The chapter title in printed colophons (daivāsura-sampad-vibhāga-yoga) is not part of this edition's segments.

original.text: arjuna uvācaye śāstravidhimutsṛjya yajante śraddhayā'nvitāḥ|teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvamāho rajastamaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna: Those who set aside the ordinance of scripture (śāstra-vidhi) yet sacrifice endowed with faith (śraddhā) — what is their standing (niṣṭhā), Kṛṣṇa: sattva, rajas or tamas?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Edition glitch: the speaker heading is fused with the first word ('arjuna uvācaye' = arjuna uvāca | ye …), kept as in the segment. The question arises from 16.23–24.

original.text: śrī bhagavānuvācatrividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā|sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śrṛṇu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: The faith (śraddhā) of embodied beings is of three kinds, born of their own nature (svabhāva): sāttvic, rājasic and tāmasic. Hear about it.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Edition glitch: heading fused ('śrī bhagavānuvācatrividhā' = śrī bhagavān uvāca | trividhā …), kept. Edition spelling 'śrṛṇu' (for śṛṇu) kept as in the segment.

original.text: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata|śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Everyone's faith accords with his being (sattva), Bhārata. This person (puruṣa) is made of faith (śraddhā-maya): whatever his faith is, that indeed he is.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Chapter 17 (Arjuna asks; Kṛṣṇa answers). Structure: (1) 17.1 Arjuna asks about those who sacrifice with faith but set aside the ordinance of scripture — is their standing sattva, rajas or tamas? (2) 17.2–6 faith is threefold, born of one's nature; the person is made of faith; the sāttvic worship the gods, the rājasic yakṣas and rākṣasas, the tāmasic the departed and spirits; those who practise terrible austerity outside scripture, tormenting the body and the Lord within it, are of demonic resolve; (3) 17.7–22 food, sacrifice, austerity and giving are each threefold: food (17.8–10); sacrifice (17.11–13); austerity of body, speech and mind (17.14–16) and its three kinds (17.17–19); giving (17.20–22); (4) 17.23–28 'oṃ tat sat' is the threefold designation of brahman: rites begin with oṃ, acts are done without aiming at fruit with 'tat' by seekers of release, 'sat' is said of being, goodness, praiseworthy acts and steadfastness in them; what is done without faith is 'asat' and worthless here and hereafter. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to answer Arjuna's question by showing that faith and every act follow the guṇas, that the sāttvic form is done as duty without desire for fruit, and that faith is indispensable.
speaker: Arjuna; Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Whether the chapter answers Arjuna's question directly (faith of those outside the ordinance is sorted by the guṇas) or by implication (such faith cannot be sāttvic, cf. 17.5–6, 17.13) is left open by the text; commentators differ.

original.text: na dveṣṭyakuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate|tyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṃśayaḥ

original.text: na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ|yastu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgītyabhidhīyate

original.text: aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam|bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit

original.text: pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha me|sāṃkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām

original.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham|vividhāśca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: The seat (adhiṣṭhāna), likewise the doer (kartṛ), the instruments (karaṇa) of various kinds, the manifold and distinct activities (ceṣṭā), and the divine (daiva) as the fifth.

original.text: śarīravāṅmanobhiryatkarma prārabhate naraḥ|nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ

original.text: tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ|paśyatyakṛtabuddhitvānna sa paśyati durmatiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: This being so, one who, because his understanding is unrefined (akṛta-buddhi), sees the self (ātman) — alone (kevala) — as the doer, that one of poor understanding does not see.

original.text: yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate|hatvāpi sa imā~llokānna hanti na nibadhyate

original.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā|karaṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ

speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ|procyate guṇasaṃkhyāne yathāvacchṛṇu tānyapi

original.text: sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvamavyayamīkṣate|avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam

original.text: pṛthaktvena tu yajjñānaṃ nānābhāvānpṛthagvidhān|vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi rājasam

original.text: yattu kṛtsnavadekasminkārye saktamahaitukam|atattvārthavadalpaṃ ca tattāmasamudāhṛtam

original.text: niyataṃ saṅgarahitamarāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam|aphalaprepsunā karma yattatsāttvikamucyate

original.text: rāgī karmaphalaprepsurlubdho hiṃsātmako'śuciḥ|harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: Relinquishing all dharmas (sarva-dharmān parityajya), come to me alone for refuge (śaraṇa). I will free you from all evils (pāpa); do not grieve.

paraphrase: Chapter 18 (Arjuna asks; Kṛṣṇa teaches; Arjuna answers; Sañjaya closes). Structure: (1) 18.1 Arjuna asks the truth of renunciation (saṃnyāsa) and relinquishment (tyāga); (2) 18.2–12 two definitions reported from the wise, two opposed views on giving up action (18.3), and Kṛṣṇa's conclusion: sacrifice, giving and austerity are not to be given up but done without attachment and fruit; relinquishment is threefold; since the embodied cannot give up action entirely, the relinquisher is the one who gives up the fruit; (3) 18.13–17 the five causes of action (declared in Sāṃkhya) and the one who, free of ego-sense, is not bound; (4) 18.18–40 the threefold impulse and composition of action and the guṇa-classification of knowledge, action, doer, understanding, steadfastness and happiness, closing with the statement that no being is free of the guṇas; (5) 18.41–48 the duties of the four classes from their own nature, perfection by worshipping with one's own work, the priority of one's own dharma; (6) 18.49–56 the sequence from unattached understanding and naiṣkarmya-siddhi through the discipline that makes one fit for becoming brahman, to supreme devotion, knowing and entering the Lord, and the eternal abode by grace for one who acts while taking refuge in him; (7) 18.57–66 direct commands to Arjuna: renounce all actions to me in thought, your nature will make you fight in any case, the Lord in the heart moves all beings, take refuge in him; then the most secret word: be mind-on-me, devoted, and — relinquishing all dharmas — come to me alone for refuge, I will free you from all evils, do not grieve; (8) 18.67–71 who may and may not be told the teaching, and the fruit of teaching, studying and hearing it; (9) 18.72–73 Kṛṣṇa's question whether the delusion is gone and Arjuna's reply that it is, that memory is regained, and that he will do Kṛṣṇa's word; (10) 18.74–78 Sañjaya's close: the wondrous dialogue heard by Vyāsa's grace, his repeated joy, and his conviction that fortune and victory are where Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna are. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to settle the question of renunciation by relinquishment of fruit within action, to sum up the teaching of action, knowledge and devotion, and to bring Arjuna from delusion to resolve.
